newsitem.title: USA: Stocks rise sharply as Greenspan eases market fears.
newsitem.headline: Stocks rise sharply as Greenspan eases market fears.

text.p: Blue-chip stocks closed sharply higher Wednesday after Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan's latest comments eased worries that the central bank might be planning some action to slow the stock market's rise.

The Dow Jones industrial average closed up 93.13 points, or 1.36 percent, at 6,945.85. In the broader market, advancing issues beat declines 1,593 to 911 on active volume of 528 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.

In his comments, Greenspan, who last week issued several unusually blunt warnings regarding stock prices during his Senate appearance, appeared to soften his tone this time in testimony before the House of Representatives.
"We don't view monetary policy as a tool to ... prick the stock market bubble, or something like that," he said.
Greenspan also repeated an assertion that the stock market was "properly priced" if Wall Street's assumptions about corporate profit growth proved correct.

The comments stood in contrast to last week, when Greenspan's testimony was peppered with reflections on speculative bubbles in the stock market. His testimony triggered an almost uninterrupted decline in stocks that pulled the Dow industrials down by 185 points in a week.
However, as he has often done in the past, Greenspan used the second session of his semi-annual report on the economy to soften his tone and markets responded with a bounce.
"He did gingerly take a step back," said Hugh Johnson, chief investment officer at First Albany Corp. "He helped us get over our jitters, and I think almost everybody is issuing a sigh of relief."

But even amid the strongest and broadest rally by stocks in three weeks, analysts cautioned that the debate on interest rates was far from over and a critical test still lay ahead with Friday's monthly payroll and wage report.
"It's all going to boil down to Friday being a pivotal day," said Bill Meehan, an analyst at Prudential Securities. "Unfortunately, no one can tell us what's going to happen then."
Analysts believe that a very strong jobs report Friday could prompt the central bank to begin raising interest rates to stem inflationary pressures before they filter through the economy.

But investors focused on the present, and as tension waned and stocks turned sharply higher, the market appeared to regain the characteristics that have served as trademarks of the most recent stage of the bull market.

"We remain in an extremely volatile market where the first tier names continue to dominate," said Scott Bleier, chief investment strategist at Prime Charter Ltd. "Corrections, when they occur in the broad indices, are very short-lived and then we're off to the races again."
The bond market also rallied, with the key 30-year Treasury bond was up more than half a point, which lowered its yield to 6.83 percent from Tuesday's close of 6.87 percent.

Drug stocks showed signs of resuming their market leadership, with several major pharmaceutical companies posting sharp gains on the session. Merck & Co. rose 3-1/4 to 94 and Pfizer Inc. added 3-5/8 to 93-3/4.
Semiconductor stocks also were sharply higher, after an influential analyst made bullish comments on the sector.
Thomas Kurlak of Merrill Lynch, said he believed a price correction in semiconductor stocks was near an end.
He also said consensus earnings estimates for two major companies in the sector, Intel Corp. and Micron Technology Inc., were too low.

Intel jumped 3-1/8 to 149-1/2 and Micron gained 2-1/2 to 42-3/8. Others in the group also rose, such as Cypress Semiconductor Corp., up 1 to 14-3/8, and National Semiconductor Corp., up 2-1/4 to 30-3/4.
Retailing stocks were also up, after several companies reported strong sales and earnings.

Dollar General Corp. climbed 2-1/4 to 31 after reporting February same-store sales, or sales from stores open at least a year, rose 11 percent vs. a year ago. Kmart Corp. added 1/8 to 13 after releasing its strongest operating results in four years.
Unison Software Inc. slid 8-1/8 to 6-1/4 after warning its quarterly results would be below Wall Street estimates. Corporate Express Inc. slid 8-3/16 to 10-1/8 on a warning of disappointing results.
The Nasdaq Composite index rose 11.72 points to 1,329.09.
The Standard & Poor's composite index of 500 stocks rose 11.04 points to 801.99. The American Stock Exchange index rose 3.84 to 600.88.
The NYSE Composite index of all listed common stocks rose 4.99 to 420.67. The average share was up 52 cents.
The Wilshire Associates Equity Index -- the market value of NYSE, American and Nasdaq issues -- was 7,658.893 up 85.487 or 1.13 percent.
